text: Nothing for months, because of the lockdown and because I was ashamed. When things opened up I saw my GP and started on an antidepressant and was referred for therapy. The therapy took a long time to start. In the meantime, I joined an online peer group for people who'd had difficult psychedelic experiences, which helped a lot. Seeing people again, getting a new job, and getting a dog were probably the biggest factors.
Ich habe einige Gespräche bei einer Psychologin geführt. Die Albträume sind weniger geworden. Segeln werde ich wohl nicht mehr.

The study team offered a debriefing and three integration sessions, which were helpful, especially because they took my experience seriously. I then saw a psychotherapist who had experience with psychedelic integration. We worked on grounding, on not ruminating about the metaphysics, and on reconnecting with my embodied life.

Reading helped, particularly philosophy of mind and accounts from other people who had difficult DMT experiences. Hiking and gardening helped a lot. Physical tasks were the best anchor.

My wife was patient and supportive throughout, which was probably the most important thing.

I briefly considered whether another, gentler psychedelic experience might help me 'complete' it. My therapist advised against it and I'm glad I listened.

Physiotherapy for the hip. I spoke with the palliative care team at my hospital about my fear of death, and a counsellor there helped me more than the mushrooms ever could. My wife and I talked a lot.

I eventually told the university, and they made the guy take the video down, but it was too late. I saw a counsellor at the student wellbeing centre, which was helpful. I transferred to a different university the next year, which was the best thing I did. I've been in therapy on and off since then for social anxiety. I'm better but still cautious.

I went back to my long-term trauma therapist, who had actually advised me against the ceremony. She didn't say 'I told you so', but I felt it anyway. We restarted weekly sessions and focused on stabilisation before going back into trauma processing. I went back on an SSRI. I also did a DBT skills group, which helped with the dissociation.

The ayahuasca organisers told me the abuser's 'energy' was leaving my body and that I needed more ceremonies. That was very harmful and I've cut all contact with them.

Yoga, specifically trauma-sensitive yoga, has been helpful. I can be in my body again a little.

I'm better than I was two years ago but still struggling.

Ich bin seit über zwei Jahren in einer Traumatherapie. Am Anfang ging es nur um Stabilisierung, weil ich so instabil war. Später haben wir mit EMDR gearbeitet, was mir geholfen hat, die Bilder etwas zu entschärfen. Ich nehme seit einem Jahr ein Antidepressivum. Mit einigen anderen Teilnehmern des Retreats stehe ich in Kontakt, wir haben eine kleine Online-Gruppe, in der wir uns austauschen. Das hilft sehr, weil sie verstehen, was passiert ist. Weniger hilfreich war die Reaktion der Organisatoren, die den Vorfall als 'tragischen Einzelfall' abgetan haben und nichts geändert haben. Ich habe immer noch Albträume, aber seltener.

I saw a counsellor for a few months. Talking to Sam helped too, hearing him joke about it made it less scary. I stopped going to raves and stopped taking any drugs. I've also done a first aid course, which made me feel less helpless.
Keine Salvia mehr. Ansonsten hat sich das von allein gegeben.
